rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one stepped bent bar, so gesture clarity and hierarchy are reasonably strong. However, the mass is still functioning mostly as a compact terraced object with only a weak ground response; the verified access edge is not clearly transformed into a public threshold, court, or undercut. In the image set the blue frontage is met by a mostly sealed side condition rather than an active entry seam, and the top/front/opposite views do not establish a convincing public void. Programmatically, neighborhood living needs an active street edge plus at least one usable void or terrace that feels occupied and socially legible. This mass is close in language to the stepped/curved neighborhood references, but it remains too object-like and too weak at the base to hard-pass as a neighborhood mixed-use/living massing.
